data.outcome_summary: The OECD Survey of Adult Skills 2023 country note for the United States reports adults’ proficiency in three domains—literacy, numeracy, and adaptive problem solving—on 500-point scales with proficiency levels (e.g., Level 1 or below; Levels 4–5). In 2022–23, U.S. adults scored 258 in literacy (near the OECD average), 249 in numeracy (below), and 247 in adaptive problem solving (below). The note quantifies distributional outcomes: 28% of adults are at Level 1 or below in literacy, 34% in numeracy, and 32% in adaptive problem solving, while 13% reach Levels 4–5 in literacy and 12% in numeracy. It also describes subgroup differences (e.g., lower proficiency among older adults) and trends over time (literacy and numeracy declines from 2012/15 to 2022–23, especially at the lower end). Methodologically, the excerpt provides survey representativeness and non-response bias checks but does not specify PV combination or missing-data handling procedures, and it does not present an ML predictive modeling pipeline.
